directory.s1: Create your business listing on {domain}, or claim the existing one.
directory.s2: Fill in the address, phone, opening hours, prices and photos.
directory.s3: Ask happy customers to leave a review there.

news.s1: Send {domain}’s editors a short note: a new service, prices or a useful tip.
news.s2: Ask to be included in price round-ups and rankings.
news.s3: Share the article on your site and social pages once it’s out.

social.s1: Create or update your official page on {domain}.
social.s2: Put your address, opening hours and prices in the profile.
social.s3: Post something useful about your services once or twice a week.

other.s1: Open {domain} and find out how businesses get added.
other.s2: Get added with accurate, complete details.
other.s3: Add a link to your website in the listing.

fact.s1: Write the correct information on your website, as text.
fact.s2: Update the same details on your 2GIS listing and other directories.
fact.s3: Find and fix pages and posts that still show the old details.

content.s1: Write a page on your site that answers these questions, in Uzbek and Russian.
content.s2: Add prices, address and opening hours to it as text.
content.s3: Link it from your site’s menu so it’s easy to find.

ai_bots_blocked.s1: Remove the Disallow lines for OAI-SearchBot and GPTBot from robots.txt.
ai_bots_blocked.s2: After the change, open yoursite.uz/robots.txt to check.
ai_bots_blocked.s3: Watch for your site among the sources after the next weekly check.

prices_as_images.s1: Write the price list on the page as text.
prices_as_images.s2: If you keep the image, add a text table next to it.
prices_as_images.s3: Update the text whenever prices change.

no_business_markup.s1: Add LocalBusiness markup to your site’s code: name, address, phone, opening hours, prices.
no_business_markup.s2: Check it with Google’s Rich Results Test.
no_business_markup.s3: Update the markup when your hours or address change.

contacts_missing.s1: Write your address, phone and opening hours as text at the bottom of every page.
contacts_missing.s2: Add a map and a landmark to the contact page.
contacts_missing.s3: Make sure 2GIS and other directories show the same details.

what.a: GEO (Generative Engine Optimization) is how visible your brand is in the answers of AI assistants like ChatGPT. When a customer asks “What’s the best clinic in Tashkent?”, the AI names a few places. GEO is the work of being one of them.

seo.q: How is this different from SEO?
seo.a: SEO is about ranking among Google’s 10 links. ChatGPT gives a ready answer with 2–3 names instead of a list of links. To be in it, the sites and directories ChatGPT relies on need correct information about you. SEO helps, but it isn’t enough.

notMentioned.q: What if ChatGPT doesn’t mention me at all?
notMentioned.a: For a small or new business that’s the most common case, and it’s exactly where to start. The check shows who ChatGPT recommends instead of you and which sites and directories it relies on. The first step is to appear there with the right details. If you’d rather not do it yourself, we do it on the Managed GEO plan.

engines.q: Which AI engines do you check?
engines.a: ChatGPT for now: through the OpenAI API with web search on, the closest method to what customers see. Yandex and Gemini are coming soon.

accuracy.a: ChatGPT answers the same question a little differently each time. That’s why we ask every question 3 times and count the share. Every report states the model and date, and you can read every answer yourself.

install.q: Do I need to install anything on my site?
install.a: No. All we need is your website address. No code, plugins or passwords.

time.q: How soon will I see results?
time.a: The free check is ready in about 2 minutes. With monitoring, a report arrives every week. Changes to your site and directory listings usually show up in ChatGPT’s answers within a few weeks.
